chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding one in Ihram who killed a locust, he said: He should feed a date, and the date is better than a locust.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for killing a locust while in Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the fidya for killing a locust during Ihram as feeding a single date, emphasizing the intrinsic value of the date over the insect. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of proportional compensation based on the creature's utility and status, distinguishing it from larger game. The narration highlights the practical application of minor penalties in Hajj rituals, ensuring the pilgrim's spiritual state is maintained through simple, accessible acts of charity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding one in Ihraam killing a locust. Heasws said: ‘He should feed dates (to a poor one), and the date is better than a locust’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following:
“About a man who kills a locust while in the state of Ihram, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He must feed a date (to a destitute person), even though a date is better than a locust.’”
